title: THE SECTOR MAP IS A CARD WITH EVERY CONTRACT ON IT
why: His answers of 10-18: Q6 (the critic must give 4 on every screen), Q7 (the style guide overrules his older layout and size orders), Q43 (a window is one centred card with an X taking nearly the whole screen) and Q1 (all contracts go on the map screen). The critic scored the map the raid opens on 2 of 5 for its art: a navy void with a thick periwinkle frame and walls, no card, header row or X, labels over their own icons, zone names dark grey on dark grey, and a grey explaining line. The map is now one charcoal card with a 1px border and a header row (the sector name and an X), zone names in light text over a dark halo, labels that keep off the marks, a glyph for each extraction ring and the hot ground, the player marker in the player colour (lime for player 1 and a solo raid, the ally blue for player 2, with a number in a two player game), a footer with the key hint and the surveyed figure, and on the opening map the start button bottom right. Every contract of the profile is listed in a column at the right with its progress and reward in $, finished ones as done; the demo hides contracts, so it lists none. The sentence what you walk stays on the map is cut. Nothing seeded moves.
now: The map you see first is a clean card with the sector name, a close button, readable zone names and every contract listed on the right.
